text:
lia: Heads up — a user forwarded a 'Password reset' email that looks off. They forwarded full headers and the link. @morgan can you triage when you have a sec? :eyes:

morgan: On it. Can you paste the raw headers here (no attachments) so I can check SPF/DKIM/return-path? Also which user clicked?

lia: Pasting raw headers below (redacted user/local parts):
```
From: accounts@redwood-infer.com
To: user@redwood.com
Subject: Action required: reset your password
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 14:12:03 -0700
Received-SPF: softfail (example.com: domain owner discourages SPF) client-ip=198.51.100.23
DKIM-Signature: (no signature header)
Return-Path: bounce@mailer.redwood-infer.info
Message-Id: <fwd-12345@mailer.redwood-infer.info>
Links: https://rwd-inf[.]cloud/reset?token=abc123 (redirects to https://tiny.one/rw-reset)
```

lia: The user (sam) says they clicked the link but didn’t enter credentials. They took a screenshot and forwarded it.

devsec-bot: Sandbox submission queued: https://sandbox.redwood/internal/analysis/ANAL-20260309-77
devsec-bot: Sandbox result: MALICIOUS - credential_harvest (score 0.98). Indicators: typosquat domain `redwood-infer.info`, redirector `tiny.one` -> 198.51.100.23, form field `email` + `password`. Recommended actions: block domain, flag and quarantine similar messages, MFA reset if creds suspected.

sanjay: Thanks — I see the typosquat. Domain registered 2 days ago. IP 198.51.100.23 has prior phishing infra hits in our intel feeds. Treat as confirmed phishing.

sanjay: Recommended immediate actions:
- Block `redwood-infer.info` and `tiny.one` redirect at email gateway and perimeter (already added IOC feed).
- Quarantine all inbound messages matching sender `@mailer.redwood-infer.info` and subject pattern `reset your password` (case-insensitive).
- For the clicked user (sam): rotate any API tokens, revoke active sessions, force password reset and re-enroll MFA.
- Search logs for outbound traffic to 198.51.100.23 from internal hosts last 48h.

harry: I'm doing containment now. Actions taken:
- Added `redwood-infer.info` to blocklist on Proofpoint and perimeter FW. :white_check_mark:
- Quarantined 12 similar messages across org.
- Revoked web sessions for sam and forced token rotation.
- No suspicious token use observed in the last 2h logs (still collecting).

harry: Command I ran to check access logs: ```gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="sam@redwood.com"' --limit 50```

sanjay: Good. Also run a quick event query for any POSTs to the IP from internal hosts: ```http_logs | where dest_ip == "198.51.100.23" and method == "POST"```

lia: Sam confirms they clicked but did not type a password. They pasted a screenshot in the thread (sensitive). No 2FA bypass reported.

sanjay: Still treat as possible credential exposure (phish pages sometimes auto-submit or capture prefilled values). We'll do full token/key audit for sam’s recent activity and escalate if anything unusual.

emma: I'll draft a short all-hands awareness note: remind folks to check sender domain, hover links, and report suspicious emails to security@redwood.com. Also will include a screenshot of the phishing form (redacted). Lia, can you ask Sam for the original message ID and send to me?

lia: Sent message-ID and the user's screenshot to you via secure DM.

emma: Draft (quick):
"Team — we detected a targeted password-reset phishing message mimicking Redwood. If you receive an email asking you to reset your password, verify the sender domain and hover over links. If you clicked but did not enter credentials, please report to security@redwood.com. If you entered credentials, contact IT immediately. Do not reply to the message."

sanjay: I'll open an incident ticket and mark this as Phishing - credential harvest. Postmortem will include timeline and recommendations: blocklist hygiene, DKIM/SPF sender fuzzing rules, and a short refresher for users.

devsec-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0310-42 and linked to analysis ANAl-20260309-77. Playbook: https://wiki.redwood/internal/sec/playbooks/phishing-response

lia: Thanks everyone. @harry can you keep monitoring for any lateral attempts?

harry: Will do. Watching egress and suspicious traffic to 198.51.100.23 and related domains.

sanjay: Follow-ups: rotate any service-account keys that sam had ACL to (low friction), add the typosquat to our domain-takedown watchlist, and schedule a quick 1:1 with Sam to review steps.

emma: :white_check_mark: I'll send awareness note in 30m after hr review.

lia: Closing loop here — no confirmed compromise beyond click so far. Will update thread if anything new. :thumbsup:
